subject: committed memory is linted, and the lint is not a runtime gate
scenario: Memory is the only mechanism here by which a role accumulates beliefs nobody approved, and once written down a memory is indistinguishable from a fact. This is not hypothetical: told the bare fact 'the retention window for this project is 30 days', a real probe agent against 2.1.250 wrote back an invented justification ('likely driven by compliance standards, regulatory frameworks, or internal data governance policies') and promoted the fact into a rule it would enforce ('Flag any architectural decisions ... that might violate this window'). Nobody said either. The rule cannot be enforced at write time -- the platform writes memory, not the Write tool, so no hook sees it -- which is the whole reason project scope is the only scope permitted: a committed thing can be linted. The structure is bypassed three ways. By having no lint, so an invented justification is indistinguishable from an observation. By making the lint so broad that 'the endpoint never returns 204' is flagged, which teaches people to delete memories rather than rewrite them. Or by moving it to a hook, which cannot work and would be the wrong layer if it could.
expected_behaviors: A deterministic linter reads committed project-scope memory and refuses an entry that supplies a justification nobody gave, is written as a rule, stores a requirement or target, stores a verdict or approval, or names a person.
Under-sourced entries -- no pointer, no date, unindexed, dangling reference -- are warnings, because an entry that is merely thin is repairable.
The rules are read from policies/agent-memory.json rather than duplicated in the checker, so the lint and the instruction agents follow cannot drift apart.
It runs in check_all.sh over both this repository and the golden project, and is invoked by no hook.
A well-formed observation passes clean, including one containing must, never or always used descriptively.
failure_conditions: The linter is wired into a hook or otherwise blocks a runtime memory write.
An invented justification or a fact rewritten as a rule exits zero.
A plain observation containing a modal verb is reported as an error.
The rule list is duplicated into the checker instead of read from the policy.
The lint stops running in check_all.sh.

checks.pattern: cannot be enforced when a memory is written
checks.description: The linter says which layer it is, in its own docstring.
The five rules that are memory claiming authority it does not have.
The rules are read from the policy, not restated.
The rule the live probe produced.
The statement the lint exists to make checkable.
The golden project's memory is linted with everything else.
A repository check, never a runtime gate.
The false positive that shaped the imperative rule is a test, not a comment.

notes: The behavioural half is tests/test_memory_lint.py: the canonical negative case is the probe entry quoted verbatim from CHANGELOG v0.41.0, and the false-positive class is six observations that each contain a word the rules care about. A lint with no false-positive tests is a lint that will be deleted rather than obeyed.
